new_entities.name: Creatine monohydrate supplementation
new_entities.description: Oral creatine monohydrate supplementation used to support training adaptations and high-intensity exercise performance.

new_entities.name: High-intensity sprint performance
new_entities.description: Performance in short, maximal, high-intensity sprint or anaerobic power tasks.

edges.effect_quant: Pooled data suggest creatine raises Wingate peak power by about 71 W, but direct sprint-race studies are not uniformly positive, especially in already elite swimmers.
edges.population: healthy adults and athletes performing short-duration maximal exercise
edges.mechanism: Creatine expands phosphocreatine availability and speeds ATP resynthesis during repeated maximal efforts, which should favor short anaerobic work. In practice, that translates more consistently to lab-based power outputs than to every sport-specific sprint outcome, where technique, training status, and event format matter a lot.
edges.summary: The literature is positive overall for anaerobic power, but less clean for real-world sprint races. Creatine seems to help some high-intensity sprint contexts, yet the effect is not universal enough to call this a straightforward protective edge without qualification.
edges.caveats: Benefit appears more reliable for cycling Wingate-type outputs and repeated sprint work than for all sport-specific sprint events. Highly trained athletes may show smaller or null improvements, and some positive results come from small trials.

evidence.notes: Creatine supplementation in young men under resistance versus non-resistance training: a systematic review and meta-analysis of strength, performance, and lean mass.

effect_quant.comparator: creatine versus control for Wingate peak power

evidence.citation: SkareOC et al 2001 Scand J Med Sci Sports
evidence.notes: Creatine supplementation improves sprint performance in male sprinters.

evidence.citation: MujikaI et al 1996 Med Sci Sports Exerc
evidence.notes: Creatine supplementation does not improve sprint performance in competitive swimmers.
